title: Micro-batch routing standup digest — Dec 02 2026
content:
Summary: Quick standing digest from the micro-batch routing working group covering the last 3 standups (11/30, 12/01, 12/02). Focus areas this sprint: (1) routing decisions for micro-batch eligibility, (2) lightweight KV prefill heuristics when batching is likely, (3) telemetry additions to measure per-route batch hit-rate and tail latency, and (4) finalizing a small kernel patch that reduces single-request scheduling overhead.

Highlights and progress:
- Routing heuristic prototype merged to feature branch (PR #789). Jonah wired the policy flags into the router pipeline; initial switch gate uses three signals: seq_len_estimate, pred_latency_budget, and cache_prefill_score.
- Tiny kernel shim (low-risk) landed on dev nodes; measured on canary: median scheduling overhead down ~9% for <32-token sequences, 95th p99 down ~6% in stable conditions. Still needs more regression runs under high concurrency.
- KV prefill heuristic experiment: Marina ran 48h A/B on staging (mixed conversational and long-context workloads). Outcome: when prefill is triggered conservatively (score threshold 0.6), effective KV reuse increases 11% and per-token compute cycles drop ~4.8% on average. However, under bursty traffic the heuristic sometimes delayed routing decisions; we logged those incidents for follow up.
- Telemetry improvements: added batch_hit_rate, prefetched_kv_misses, route_fallback_count metrics. Sam instrumented the tracing spans to include route_reason. These are visible in the 'micro-batch' dashboard (linked in artifacts).

Open issues and anomalies:
- Prefill-induced routing delay: observed ~120ms occasional stalls when prefill kicked in for short-lived sessions. Root cause likely contention where prefill waits on an async cache-write; Diego suggested switching to write-behind pattern for the small object path. Action: Diego to prototype write-behind by next Wed (12/08).
- Heuristic sensitivity: current thresholds tuned to reduce false-positives, but that also underutilizes batching on some chat workloads. Need a simple auto-calibration pass. Action: Jonah + Marina to run adaptive-threshold sweep across customer-like traffic by 12/09.
- Kernel fallback path: fallback to the legacy scheduler is happening more for sequences >256 tokens when the new kernel chooses micro-batch lanes; investigate compatibility checks. Action: Aisha to open SRV-1289 and assign to kernel team.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Rollout cadence: keep kernel shim on canary for two more weeks, do not enable on dedicated pools until we have one week of stable p99 results across peak hour tests.
- Prefill conservative mode = default for next 2 sprints. Opt-in aggressive mode via config flag for teams wanting to experiment.
- Telemetry retention for micro-batch metrics set to 45 days for faster iteration.

Short notes / to-self fragments (informal):
- "need a small table showing diff by workload type (chat vs longform) — include median/p95/p99 and cost delta" (Jonah)
- "check recent outage blips on 2026-11-27 — might be unrelated but look at prefill queue length at that time" (Marina)
- "Add example config to README for enabling aggressive prefill per-route" (Sam)

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego: prototype write-behind small-object prefill path and bench vs current approach — due 2026-12-08.
- Jonah + Marina: run adaptive-threshold sweep, produce tuning table and recommended defaults — due 2026-12-09.
- Aisha: file SRV-1289 (kernel scheduling fallback investigation) and triage with kernel leads — due 2026-12-03.
- Sam: finalize dashboard panels and add alert for prefetched_kv_misses > 500/min — due 2026-12-06.
- All: consolidate notes into the micro-batch RFC draft for review next Tues (2026-12-08).

Meeting artifacts and refs:
- Short clip of the canary run uploaded to the team drive (link in linked_artifacts).
- Heatmap exported of per-route batch hit-rate across 11/25–11/30; see Confluence page.

Unresolved questions for next sync:
- Is write-behind safe for multi-tenant caching semantics (race conditions)? If not, what mutex strategy is acceptable given latency SLOs?
- Should we add a short-circuit for sessions with predicted session-length < 3 requests to avoid prefill entirely?

Quick retrospective (what went well / what to improve):
- Went well: rapid iteration on telemetry gave us actionable signals within 48 hours. Kernel shim yielded measurable wins quickly. Cross-discipline pairing (infra + kernel + routing) sped up triage loops.
- Improve: need a more robust canary test harness to simulate bursty traffic; current staging mixes traffic but doesn't reproduce real spike patterns. Next sprint we schedule a synthetic spike series.

Callouts:
- Customer Impact: none observed in production; dedicated pools unaffected. Keep alerting on route_fallback_count until kernel patch is GA.
- Slack threads: major discussion in #runtime-kv about prefill semantics — link above.

End of digest. If you want a one-pager summary for PMs/solutions, I can trim this down to bullets and impact numbers by EOD 12/03. — Aisha
